title: Empty Unix records evade capacity accounting or readiness
mechanism: MessageQueue::try_send charges only payload bytes to total_length, so zero-length datagrams (optionally carrying SCM_RIGHTS files) queue without bound. Connected::try_write records empty seqpacket records outside the byte ring and Connected::check_io_events ignores them for IN readiness.
contract: Every queued Unix datagram or seqpacket record consumes bounded buffer accounting even with zero payload, and a queued empty seqpacket record makes the socket readable (Linux af_unix.c, unix_dgram_poll).
observed: Source only: empty datagrams add zero to the queue charge and never hit a bound, and an empty seqpacket record does not set IN readiness.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an empty-datagram send loop on a nonblocking socketpair and a poll after one empty seqpacket send.

caveats: Source-only lead: queue bounds and zero-length seqpacket readability not tested. Brief CR-2 covers AST-33 and AST-34, while report CR-2 is AST-40.
